hypotheses.observation: Built, off (SITEMAP_GUESS_RULE = False). Runs sg1-cohort/dev2/dev3/dev4 (no search, --sitemap-guess-cap) and the recorded guard rp-sg1-dev4, backend/evaluation/research/runs/2026-10-17/LOOP_REPORT.md 2026-10-20 11:00. Hit/wrong/related/missed unchanged on every set (cohort 4/0/0/6, dev2 2/0/1/7, dev3 5/0/0/9, dev4 1/0/0/8; guard 5/0/1/3 in both on columns); no wrong page, no hit lost; most hosts 2-8 s faster (cohort ubc -22 s, ntu -15 s, kaist -5 s). But the pre-registered ctu saving did not appear (-6 s against -20 to -30 s), there is no stable gain, and dev3 shows a stable claim loss (unsw ielts.overall, ielts.subscores): unsw finishes at 116/118 s off and 119/119 s on, and both on captures end CAPTURE_IN_PROGRESS under the 120 s case clock, so their claims are dropped whole; the pages read are the same. Verdict: SG-1 stays off (13-Q2 gate). The clock-edge loss is a harness fragility rather than a rule effect, left to the planner as a follow-up. case_ids lists the cohort cases whose seconds moved most; the development cases are named in this observation.
hypotheses.proposed_rule: When robots.txt names no sitemap and the host asks a crawl delay of at least SLOW_HOST_SECONDS, guess only /sitemap.xml; on any host, stop guessing after SITEMAP_GUESS_MAX_404 consecutive guesses answered 404.
hypotheses.counterexample: unsw (dev3): a case running at 116-119 s crosses the 120 s clock by a second and loses every claim it had extracted, so a time-saving rule can still show a claim loss.
hypotheses.falsification: Pre-registered (docs/process/NEXT_CYCLES_2026-10-23.md §4, SG-1 verdict row): ctu case_time -20 to -30 s; kit, itu, msu, um, ethz, utokyo -3 to -6 s; hits unchanged everywhere, 0 wrong, guard identical -> on by default; a hit lost or a wrong page -> stays off. Not met (no ctu saving, a stable claim loss on dev3). Worth a re-run once a capture that crosses the case clock no longer drops its claims whole.
